summary: Orléans is a bag-building worker placement game where you draft followers into a bag, then draw a handful each round to place on action spaces and trigger their effects. It rewards efficient engine-building across trade, science, and exploration tracks, with a calm, low-conflict feel punctuated by tense event cards that can wreck an unprepared player.
praised: Elegant bag-building mechanism that feels fresh compared to standard worker placement
Multiple viable paths to victory with satisfying engine-building
Tight, clean rules that produce deep strategic decisions
criticised: Very low direct player interaction, can feel solitaire-ish
Event deck can deliver harsh, sometimes 'gotcha' setbacks
Downtime between turns in higher player counts
Some randomness in the bag draw can feel swingy for a euro

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with some space competition and trade route/knight-based blocking

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple tracks (science, trade stations, finances, development) so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient multi-track engine rather than one dominant source
